top_signals.title: The Axis of Upheaval Goes to War
top_signals.summary: Andrea Kendall-Taylor and Richard Fontaine, former members of the National Security Council, argue that the members of what they call the “axis of upheaval”—Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea—are deepening their cooperation. Meanwhile, Washington is creating friction with many of its own partnerships. If these developments continue unabated, the United States will squander the strength of its network just as its adversaries learn to make the most of theirs.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: S&P 500 Suffers Worst Week Since June as AI Fears Hit Chipmakers
top_signals.summary: The S&P 500 Index dropped on Friday to cap its biggest weekly loss since June, as a spike in crude prices renewed inflation fears while worries about the viability of the artificial intelligence trade pressured chipmakers.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Big Tech stocks suffer biggest weekly drop since ‘liberation day’
top_signals.summary: AI trade jitters send investors scrambling for government debt in a move that halts a months-long Treasury sell-off
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Big US Bank Stocks Log Worst Weekly Losing Streak Since 2008
top_signals.summary: Big US bank shares recorded their worst weekly losing streak since the 2008 Global Financial Crisis after quarterly earnings didn’t do enough to lift sentiment for the ailing sector.

top_signals.title: The Nuclear Deal That Could Save NATO
top_signals.summary: Former U.S. NATO ambassador Ivo Daalder argues that the scramble to shore up Europe's conventional defense risks overlooking the continent's greatest security weakness: nuclear deterrence. Europe knows it can't fully trust Washington's guarantee anymore. But he lays out a middle path between dependence and nuclearization that would extend France's and the United Kingdom's nuclear umbrella—a course, he argues, that could even repair the transatlantic alliance.
